source_spans.locator: Trends in Cognitive Sciences 7(3), published p.134, Abstract: responses are slower and usually more error-prone immediately after a task change; advance preparation reduces but does not eliminate the switch cost

Trends in Cognitive Sciences 7(3), published pp.135-136, basic phenomena and paradigms: switch, preparation, residual, and mixing costs; preparation interval manipulations and separation of active preparation from passive dissipation

Trends in Cognitive Sciences 7(3), published pp.135-137, candidate sources of transition costs: time-consuming endogenous task-set reconfiguration, transient persistence of prior activation/inhibition, and longer-term associative retrieval/priming

Trends in Cognitive Sciences 7(3), published p.137, synthesis: multiple causes are likely; the exact blend is disputed, transient carry-over is an established contributor, and the preparation effect is commonly attributed to time-consuming endogenous reconfiguration

Trends in Cognitive Sciences 7(3), published pp.138-139, neuroimaging/TMS discussion: differential activation on changed versus repeated trials does not by itself distinguish controlling regions from controlled targets

conditions: human participants perform a small set of simple stimulus-response tasks in sequences containing both task repetitions and task changes

some paradigms provide advance knowledge and vary the time available before the upcoming stimulus, allowing partial preparation while also potentially allowing passive decay of the prior configuration
population: human participants in the behavioral and neuropsychological task-transition literature reviewed by the source
task: perform the currently required simple classification or response rule while occasionally changing from the rule used on the preceding trial
temporal_scope: immediate trial-to-trial history determines whether the current task repeats or changes, and advance preparation can occur before current-stimulus onset
carry-over from prior configurations can persist transiently across trials and, through associative retrieval or priming, over longer intervals

nodes.description: task-specific configuration active or recently active before the current trial
task-specific configuration required for the current trial
whether the current trial requires repeating the preceding task configuration or changing to another one
foreknowledge and time available before current-stimulus onset to prepare the required configuration
response latency and error probability on the current trial
slower and/or less accurate performance on a changed-task trial relative to a repeated-task trial
remaining changed-versus-repeated performance difference after substantial advance preparation
time-consuming internally driven process that prepares or establishes the currently required task configuration
short-lived persistence of activation or inhibition associated with the previously performed task configuration
longer-lived associative retrieval or priming of competing task configurations by stimuli or recent experience
family of behavioral paradigms comparing changed-task with repeated-task trials while varying predictability, cue timing, and advance preparation

relations.description: performance is generally slower and often more error-prone immediately after a task change than after a task repetition
providing foreknowledge and more time for advance preparation usually reduces the transition-related performance decrement

the remaining decrement after preparation is not attributed to a single source; the review treats transient prior-state carry-over and update processes that cannot always be completed before stimulus onset as contributors whose exact blend remains unsettled

the review treats the observed transition-related decrement as multiply determined rather than as evidence for a single control mechanism, with both internally driven updating and carry-over at more than one timescale contributing in different paradigms
when advance information is available, part of the internally driven configuration update can occur before the current stimulus and response
the behavioral paradigms expose both the immediate changed-versus-repeated performance difference and the portion that remains after extended preparation
